summary: Compose a section as foreground edge, cut surface, revealed interior and retained context so depth relationships stay readable while the intact model and section state remain recoverable.
objective: A cutaway tells where the cut occurs, what material it crosses and how the revealed parts continue in depth without presenting renderer clipping as a physical removal.
applies_when: A section or cutaway must explain nested spatial relationships.
A clipping plane alone produces a technically open view but weak depth order or ambiguous cut surfaces.
intent_signals: compose a cutaway with readable depth layers
show foreground cut edge and interior context
example_prompts: Compose a house section with cut walls, room depth and an exterior context strip.
Stage an anatomical section so the cut surface, deeper organs and retained body outline remain distinguishable.
negative_signals: Deleting the front geometry and losing the intact state.
Using identical contrast for cut surfaces and deep background parts.
not_for: The renderer API for clipping planes and caps.
Measured scientific slicing or segmentation validation.

principles: Treat the section plane as a compositional boundary. Give the cut surface, first revealed layer, deeper context and exterior remainder distinct but related roles.
Preserve enough continuation cues—edges, supports, lumens, routes or silhouette—to show how revealed parts connect beyond the cut.
Decide whether the view is an explanatory lens over intact lighting/physics or depicts removed material; align shadows, caps and language with that decision.
implementation: In Blender, keep intact source collections and author section-ready interiors, thickness and candidate cameras. Use a duplicate presentation collection only when destructive authoring is unavoidable and label it as such.

In Three.js, delegate plane mechanics to the related clipping adapter. Compose a cap/edge treatment, depth contrast, context shell and label exclusions around the runtime plane; glTF does not transport the active section state.
Provide a plane indicator or section title and reset. Do not let clipped render visibility change quantities, colliders or source geometry unless a separate model operation owns that change.
observable_checks: Move the section through a junction: the cut location and material thickness remain legible, deeper parts do not masquerade as cut faces, and continuity cues persist.
Disable the section and compare world transforms, quantities and colliders with the intact state; they remain unchanged for a display-only section.
From the authored camera and one oblique inspection angle, the viewer can distinguish foreground cut, revealed layer and retained context without relying on color alone.

creative_affordances: Use poche, hatching, glow edges, ghosted shells or restrained exploded offsets as long as their meaning is stated.
A fixed dollhouse cut can be stronger than a movable plane for a single narrative shot.
known_limits: Clipping does not create caps or reconstruct hidden interiors; those require authored geometry or a separate rendering method.
No section, shadow, cap or reset behavior was rendered.

claims.statement: Three.js material clipping planes are world-space planes that discard negative signed-distance fragments, require WebGLRenderer local clipping for material planes, and expose separate intersection and shadow-clipping controls.
claims.scope: Render clipping only; capping, depth hierarchy, object continuity and collider behavior are outside this API.
